title.narrative: Community Partnerships to Strengthen Sustainable Development (COMPASS)

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): COMPASS will enhance the management of forests and natural resources in Bangladesh. The activity will continue to train youth conservation corps, provide technical assistance to the Bangladesh Forest Department (BFD), develop capacity for academia, and pilot innovative tools for forest research and management in partnership with NGOs and Community Based Organizations (CBOs). The United States Forest Service (USFS) will build on previous experience in Bangladesh, supporting unique needs of the sector and factoring in competitive advantages. Using FY 2024 funding, COMPASS will scale up the youth conservation corps and incorporate sustainable and cost effective approaches and provide soft and vocational skills targeted to achieve employment and environmental stewardship. It will strengthen community institutional capacities and provide skill development support for alternative livelihoods aiming for forest landscape restoration. COMPASS will provide refresher and advanced statistics and programming training to BFD officials to use geospatial tools for forest monitoring and management and facilitate the formulation of the forest ecosystem valuation methodology. It will enhance the capacity of academia to do advanced research on forest management through knowledge exchange, technology transfer, and pilot new tools like i-Tree Eco for urban greenspace management. Its forest landscape restoration (FLR) interventions will increase the absorptive and adaptive capacity of the indigenous communities in Bandarban facing climate risks. This activity aligns with the priorities of the Government of Bangladesh in achieving its REDD+ objectives. Through advancing forest monitoring and management technologies, the activity contributes to the U.S. government's priority of combating global climate change and the U.S. Embassy's goal of making Bangladesh a socially and environmentally resilient country. Funding contributes to SL Indirect ($500k), GE/ WE Secondary ($600k)
